text: Lesson 10 got Claude generating validated SQL against your schema. But a real question often needs something the database was never going to contain -- a live exchange rate, current weather, a geocoded address. 'What's this month's revenue in euros?' needs a SQL aggregate and a live rate -- SQL alone can't answer it.

The cleanest way to combine them isn't hardcoding 'always call the API after the query' -- it's giving Claude a second tool and letting it orchestrate, the same multi-tool pattern from the AI Agents course. Add a get_exchange_rate tool alongside run_sql_query. With both in the tools array, Claude can query the database, see the result, then call the API in a follow-up turn, and combine both in its final answer.

A live HTTP call can time out, rate-limit you, or return a bad status, and your code has to handle that, not the model. A real version sets a timeout, checks the response status, and backs off and retries on a 429 rather than crashing the tool call.

If a SQL result has 200 rows and each needs a currency lookup, calling the API once per row is 200 requests for maybe 3 or 4 distinct currencies. Deduplicate the values you actually need, cache the lookup for the request, and batch if the API supports it. It's the same N-plus-1 problem from database code, just moved to the API boundary.
With both the database and a live API working together under Claude's own orchestration, Lesson 12 wraps up Project 2 -- packaging what you've built into something you can actually present.
